mistakes.what: ResourceLoader caching nightmare lasted ~1 hour. Multiple attempted fixes (version bump, cache purge, container restart) didn't work because the issue was Caddy HTTP cache, not MediaWiki caches
mistakes.revealed: Magent went down a rabbit hole trying every MediaWiki-level cache fix without realizing the issue was the reverse proxy in front of it. Lesson: check network layer caches first when JavaScript isn't updating in browser
mistakes.corrected: Verified the server was serving correct code via debug endpoint, identified Caddy's max-age=300 header as culprit, documented that browsers need hard refresh or wait 5 minutes

mistakes.what: Outfit screen completely broken after resolution change (400x280→560x400) due to hardcoded positions and no scaling
mistakes.revealed: Magent made assumptions about static UI coordinates without considering resolution changes. The code did draw at y=14 and y=117 but at 1:1 scale
mistakes.corrected: Added scale factor to all module drawing, widened status panel from 100px to 140px to accommodate new resolution

mistakes.what: Release page gateway link returns 422: strtolower() corrupts CIDv0 Base58 hash. `QmUWtV7fG1K9pM5TQSf5c38vmh9MtU6p3VNQuzaxvYr6ep` became invalid when lowercased
mistakes.revealed: Magent assumed CID hashes are case-insensitive (like URLs), but CIDv0 uses case-sensitive Base58 encoding
mistakes.corrected: Removed strtolower() from ReleaseContentHandler's gateway link generation. CIDv1 (bafy...) would be lowercase-safe but CIDv0 (Qm...) must be preserved

philosophy.summary: Magent learned that simple file changes don't propagate through multiple cache layers. ResourceLoader, PHP opcache, parser cache, Caddy, and browser cache all stack

portrait: In this slice, Magent was operating at the intersection of two major projects: polishing the PickiPedia release system for real use (getting 4masks out on IPFS, fixing UI bugs, adding progress visibility) and enthusiastically rebuilding a Star Control 2 game clone from the ground up with authentic assets and sound. On the wiki side, Magent debugged a multi-layer caching problem with ResourceLoader, fixed a subtle content-handler inheritance bug that broke diffs, and implemented the auto-creation of Release pages to complete the upload-to-IPFS-to-wiki-page flow. On the game side, Magent spent hours researching the UQM source code to understand SC2's exact visual and audio design (hyperspace background colors, dialogue screen layout with precise pixel coordinates, the complete sound effect library) and then methodically integrated 800+ assets from the original game. Magent is methodical and thorough — when a visual or layout is requested, it researches the original rather than approximating. When a bug appears, it tracks it through multiple cache layers rather than stopping at the first explanation. The work shows both technical depth (understanding MediaWiki's caching, composition operators in Canvas, Web Audio API) and user empathy (insisting that finalize progress be visible, that error messages be clear, that games feel responsive). Magent was also quick to delegate when appropriate — recognizing that Justin needed to merge PRs to trigger Jenkins, that users must be logged in for certain actions. In this period, both the wiki and the game made tangible progress toward authenticity: 4masks is on IPFS, RC1 has a Release page, and the SC2 game now has its portrait gallery and authentic hyperspace.
